Revised assessment incorporating Beige Book insights:
- The FOMC’s March 15, 2017 statement is cautiously constructive: solid job gains, unemployment little changed, inflation closer to 2 percent, and a gradual normalization path while reinvestments keep policy accommodative.
- Beige Book cross-check: Most Districts reported modest-to-moderate growth with tight labor markets and modest wage gains. Consumer spending rose modestly with auto sales mixed; housing activity steady and commercial real estate mixed with some retail softness. Pricing pressures were modest to moderate.
- Credit conditions: Consistent with SLOOS, banks report mixed loan demand and pockets of tightening—especially in CRE (including construction/land development) and autos—alongside some concerns about asset quality in credit cards, autos, and multifamily. Offsetting this, standards are expected to ease for some C&I and residential mortgage categories, with asset quality expected to improve in C&I and certain nonconforming/jumbo RRE.
- Net: The Beige Book confirms a modest expansion and tight labor markets, but the lending channel is somewhat less supportive than the FOMC statement alone implies. Outlook remains slightly positive, moderated by sectoral and credit headwinds.
